headline: Copper overtakes iron ore as the top earnings driver
summary_short: BHP's FY2026 (year ended 30 June 2026) underlying EBITDA rose 27% y/y to $32.9B and attributable profit after tax rose 9% y/y to $9,833M, with copper becoming the single largest earnings contributor for the first time (>$18B, 54% of Group EBITDA).
summary_long: Full-year underlying EBITDA of $32.9B (+27% y/y from $26B) and attributable profit of $9,833M (+9% y/y) were driven by copper, which overtook iron ore as the largest earnings contributor — over $18B of Underlying EBITDA, 54% of the Group total — on a second consecutive year of ~2Mt copper production. Iron ore (WAIO) posted record production and shipments while holding its cost position; coal was also reported stronger. The board declared a $0.99/share fully franked final dividend (72% payout ratio). Management reiterated a growth strategy targeting ~50% higher copper production by the mid-2030s, with the Vicuña Stage I project (Argentina) having cleared regulatory milestones toward a possible final investment decision by end-2026.
